text:
sam: heads-up — recent k6 replay runs are showing sustained backpressure on the ingest worker when we hit ~1.8k rps, causing the procfile-managed k6 process to get OOM/killed on the node.

mike: ugh. any obvious OOM in dmesg or kube events?

sam: dmesg shows the cgroup oom killer hitting node-exporter container sometimes but mostly the k6 worker itself shows java/lang: OutOfMemory in the pod logs (heap dump snippet attached to logs).

jess: is this the bucketed traffic replay config we used last week? thought we capped concurrency there.

sam: same replay script, but we changed the sample rate to 100% and increased VU count. Also noticed the Procfile launcher we use doesn't pass --max-old-space-size, so Node k6 runner grows.

carmen: ok two axes: tune the replay (rate limiting + batching) and fix the procfile/service to pin memory. can we try a quick experiment with --vus 400 --duration 15m and k6 option --rps 1800?

sam: want to run that tomorrow AM in staging. @mike can you add a systemd wrapper that sets NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048 for the k6 runner and ensure restart=on-failure? something like:

```
[Unit]
Description=k6 replay runner
After=network.target

[Service]
Environment=NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/k6 run /srv/replays/current/script.js --vus 400 --duration 15m --out influxdb=http://localhost:8086
Restart=on-failure
LimitNOFILE=65536

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

mike: will do. also adding a throttling decorator in the replay controller so we can soft-limit burst when queue depth > 1000.

replay-bot: Started replay run 1851234567-01 in staging (vus=400, target_rps=1800) — logs: https://ci.internal/replays/1851234567-01

jess: during the run, can we capture pprof + flamegraph for the k6 process and the ingest worker? if we can get cpu/mem profiles at the peak we can see the hot alloc path.

sam: yes — I'll attach the profiler script to the replay job. it will run `curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > /tmp/k6-pprof.pb` then upload.

carmen: timeline: systemd wrapper + throttling patch merged by EOD, staging run tomorrow 09:00 PT, collect profiles, then decision to either reduce sample rate or scale the ingest pool for weekend soak. sound ok?

mike: yep I'm on the systemd change and will cut the PR now. ping me in the morning for the deploy. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all — will post results & flamegraphs here once uploaded.

jess: nice. if it still blows up, we should try switching the k6 runner to the go binary instead of node wrapper (lighter memory profile).

sam: noted — fallback plan B.
